newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Kekkuti sees rising exports, seeks listing.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Kekkuti sees rising exports, seeks listing.

text.p: Hungarian mineral water bottler and distributor Kekkuti Asvanyviz Rt plans to increase exports and list its shares, the company said on Wednesday.
"Exports accounted for about half a percent of last year's sales revenue. This proportion will rise to seven to eight percent," Kekkuti said in a statement.
For 1996 the company forecasts sales revenues of 1.2 billion forints, up from 850 million in 1995.
Kekkuti has built what it called substantial export markets in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and has also delivered smaller amounts to Argentina.
Kekkuti had hoped to deliver to IFOR Bosnian peacekeeping forces based in Hungary but these deals failed apart from a few test deliveries, it said.
"The reason was not the quality or the price of Kekkuti mineral water but the fact that Germany has remained the main supply base for military forces stationed here," it said.
Increasing exports offset declining domestic demand, Kekkuti said, adding that it expected to maintain its over 20 percent market share this year.

The company, which is 70 percent owned by U.K.-based Lucienne Ltd, confirmed its earlier plans to seek a listing on the Budapest Stock Exchange in November. It would be the first mineral water company to do so.
Of the remaining shares, 28.8 percent are held by Merrill Lynch, while employees hold 1.4 percent.
